BASE: written on 0105 and merged (merge commits, nothing rebased) onto staging 605e971e, which carries 0106_ocr_worker_account.sql and 0107_ocr_page_allowance.sql, and then onto staging 6aae042e, which adds 0108_records_processing_cover_lifetime.sql (all three signed); it applies after 0108 and uses nothing 0106, 0107 or 0108 adds. 0106 only inserts two rows (the OCR worker's account and role), 0107 only adds objects in schema ocr and replaces ocr.validate_job_write, and 0108 only replaces identity.records_processing_direct_care_cover and its comment; none changes any body, policy, column, key or row-level security setting 0115 pins (outreach.context_allows, outreach.registration_campaign_member, auth.membership_has_permission, the platform session helpers and platform.reject_mutation, the policies of outreach.registration_cases and outreach.campaign_members). The nine body pins were re-measured after the 6aae042e merge on a fresh 0001-0108 database and are unchanged (auth.membership_has_permission 65e3eaff93fe729fd5c5b986b80c9dd6, the same md5 0108 itself pins), so no pin changed and 0115 is byte-identical to the file reviewed on 0105 (same sha256). runtime-grants.sql is 6aae042e's file (0108 does not change it) with the 0115 block after 0107's block, so its sha256 here covers both and is unchanged by this merge. In plain words, applying 0115 to production does this. It adds two new Outreach tables and two name readers and changes nothing that exists. Field officers can record a visit, referral or follow-up on a registration (outreach.registration_case_visits); only staff who may already read that registration at that clinic, and for a campaign registration only members of that campaign, can read or add them, and nobody can change or delete one. A small log (outreach.link_preview_attempts) holds only ids and a time for each Health ID check, so outreach-api can stop a member after 20 checks an hour; it never holds the Health ID. Two readers give the staff name (and nothing else) of the person who registered a case, and of campaign members who share a campaign with the caller, at the caller's clinic only, at most 200 at a time, without locking any row. The Outreach runtime gets read and insert on the two tables and may run the two readers, in the migration (for roles that already exist) and in runtime-grants.sql (its 0115 block), identically; nothing is granted to PUBLIC. Nothing is used until outreach-api's OUTREACH_VISITS_ENABLED is turned on; today's image calls none of it. Locks, measured with pg_locks before commit on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16.15 copy migrated through 0105 by a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS owner (before the merge): SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE on outreach.registration_cases and identity.staff_facility_memberships (the new foreign keys), taken NOWAIT every 10 ms for at most 5 seconds; ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on the new tables and their indexes; the catalogs' own locks; no other application table. The whole apply took 7 ms; with a writer holding outreach.registration_cases it stopped after 5.1 s with 55P03 and applied nothing. Proof: the suite services/ehr-api/test/database/outreach-visits.integration.sql (59 cases) passes on a fresh superuser-migrated database (readers lent to an owner without BYPASSRLS) and on an upgrade from 0105 in production shape (owner hid_migrator, NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS). PROVED after the merge of staging 6aae042e on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16.15 with pgvector (created and deleted): FRESH install of all 110 files 0001-0108 and 0115 by the superuser runner (plan 110 pending, dry run rolled back, apply, role bootstrap and verification pass, 0 pending), the nine 0115 body pins re-measured unchanged, the 0115 suite 59 cases pass and all 82 database suites pass; UPGRADE in production shape: a database built by staging 6aae042e's own runner, files and runtime-grants.sql with owner hid_migrator (NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS, MIGRATION_TARGET=rds; 109 files, ledger last 0108), the 0115 suite fails there, plan 1 pending (0115 with this sha256), dry run rolled back with no 0115 object, apply, 0 pending, the runner again applies nothing, the 0115 ACLs after the migration equal those after a role bootstrap with this runtime-grants.sql, role verification passes, the 0115 suite passes (59 cases, readers run as their owner hid_migrator); services/ehr-api/scripts/test-staging-schema-upgrade.mjs passed with HID_BASELINE_RUNTIME_GRANTS set to 6aae042e's runtime-grants.sql (baseline 109 files, 110 integrated, declared exactly 0115; dry run rolled back, checksums kept, migration grants match runtime-grants.sql (2611), 188 row-security settings unchanged, migrator not superuser and not BYPASSRLS).
